label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the uploaded text on "\n" only (`text.split("\n")`), so it doesn't strip a trailing "\r" when the file uses Windows-style CRLF line endings. The new accounting export tool on Windows likely produces CRLF files, so the last column name in the header (and the last field of every data row) ends up with a trailing "\r" attached, e.g. "description\r" instead of "description".

Because `assertShape` checks `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some((column) => !header.includes(column))`, the mangled last header column no longer matches "description", so `missingRequired` is true and an `IngestError("errors.rowShape", { row: index + 1 })` is thrown immediately while parsing the header line (index 0), which is why it always reports "row 1" regardless of the actual file contents.

The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip a trailing "\r" from each line, or split on /\r?\n/) before splitting into header/rows.

The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip a trailing "\r" from each line, or split on /\r?\n/) before splitting into header/rows.
